---
title: "Vietnam measles serology: overview of data and some results"
format: html
editor: visual
editor_options: 
  chunk_output_type: console
---


```{r include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE)

if (grepl("arc|hoisy", Sys.getenv("USER"))) {
  path2data <- paste0("~/Library/CloudStorage/OneDrive-OxfordUniversityClinical",
                      "ResearchUnit/GitHub/choisy/measles serology/")
}
path2cache <- paste0(path2data, "cache/")
make_path <- function(x) paste0(path2cache, x)
readRDScache <- function(x) readRDS(make_path(x))
```

::: {.callout-note}
Full analysis (with R code): [https://choisy.github.io/measles_serology](https://choisy.github.io/measles_serology)

GitHub repository: [https://github.com/choisy/measles_serology](https://github.com/choisy/measles_serology)

Leave comments or make suggestions by posting an issue [here](https://github.com/choisy/measles_serology/issues) (click on the green button in the top right corner).
:::

The locations of provinces on the map:

![Sampled provinces in red. Only December 2019 for Kien Giang in orange.](index_files/figure-html/fig-map-1.png){#fig-map width=470px}

The number of samples per time point per province:

```{r}
readRDScache("nb_samples_prov_timepoint.rds")
```

![Number of samples as a function of collection time.](index_files/figure-html/fig-sampling_intensity-1.png){#fig-sampling_intensity width=537.5px}

![Number of samples as a function of collection time and province.](index_files/figure-html/fig-nb_sample_day_site-1.png){#fig-nb_sample_day_site width=537.5px}

![Age distribution of samples per province and time point. The red lines show the target: 5 samples per 1-year age class from 0 to 20 year old and 10 samples per 5-year age class from 20 to 70 year old.](index_files/figure-html/fig-nb_samples_site_timepoint_ageclass-1.png){#fig-nb_samples_site_timepoint_ageclass width=672px}

![Sex distribution per province and time point (pink: females, blue: males).](index_files/figure-html/fig-sex_distribution-1.png){#fig-sex_distribution width=470px}

![Distribution of titers on a decimal logarithm scale with the 2 thresholds from the manufacturer for interpretation: <150 IU is negative (red), >200 IU is positive (green) and between 150 and 200 IU is equivocal (orange).](index_files/figure-html/fig-distribution_titers-1.png){#fig-distribution_titers width=537.5px}

![Distribution of titers on a decimal logarithm scale with the 2 thresholds from the manufacturer for interpretation: <150 IU is negative (red), >200 IU is positive (green) and between 150 and 200 IU is equivocal (orange). The 3 time points are shown chronologically from top to bottom.](index_files/figure-html/fig-distribution_titers_timepoints-1.png){#fig-distribution_titers_timepoints width=376px}

![Seroprevalence per age class, using the 200 IU as a threshold, with 95% confidence intervals.](index_files/figure-html/fig-age_profile-1.png){#fig-age_profile width=537.5px}

![Seroprevalence per age class, using the 200 IU as a threshold, with 95% confidence intervals. The 3 time points are shown chronologically from top to bottom.](index_files/figure-html/fig-age_profile_timepoints-1.png){#fig-age_profile_timepoints width=376px}

![Same as @fig-age_profile_timepoints shown differently: each panel is an age class from younger to older from top left to bottom right.
